problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨z,\,-y,\,4x+3⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined in Cartesian coordinates as $z=x+2y+1$ for $0\le x\le 2$ and $0\le y\le 1.$ Calculate the flux of $F$ through $S$ with respect to the upward-pointing unit normal vector $n.$

*Hint: You're given that the fundamental vector product of $S$ with respect to its canonical parametrization is $||{r}_{x}\times {r}_{y}||=\sqrt{6}.$*

feedback.problem: Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨x+3,\,x+y,\,z-x+6⟩$ and a finite region $S$ of the plane $z=x-y$ such that $\text{Area}(S)=\sqrt{6}.$ Calculate the flux of $F$ through $S$ with respect to the upward-pointing unit normal vector $n.$
feedback.worked_solution:
If $S$ is an oriented surface with unit normal vector $n,$ and $F$ is continuous vector field, then the flux of $F$ across $S$ measured with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S.
$$

Notice that our surface $z=x-y$ can be written using the dot product as 

$$
⟨x,\,y,\,z⟩\cdot {{⟨-1,\,1,\,1⟩}_{⏟}}_{\overset{~}{n}}=0,\,\text{or}\,⟨x,\,y,\,z⟩\cdot {{⟨1,\,-1,\,-1⟩}_{⏟}}_{-\overset{~}{n}}=0.
$$

Since we require an upward-pointing normal vector to our surface $S,$ we must select one where the $z$-component is positive. This gives us the normal vector

$$
\overset{~}{n}=⟨-1,\,1,\,1⟩.
$$

Normalizing this vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =\frac{\overset{~}{n}}{‖\overset{~}{n}‖} \\  & =\frac{⟨-1,\,1,\,1⟩}{\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨-1,\,1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the fact that $z=x-y$ on $S,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F\cdot n & =⟨x+3,\,x+y,\,z-x+6⟩\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨-1,\,1,\,1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨x+3,\,x+y,\,6-y⟩\cdot ⟨-1,\,1,\,1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}(-(x+3)+(x+y)+(6-y)) \\  & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{3}} \\  & =\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the flux of $F$ across $S$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{S}\sqrt{3}\,\text{d}S \\  & =\sqrt{3}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S \\  & =\sqrt{3}\cdot \text{Area}(S) \\  & =\sqrt{3}\cdot \sqrt{6} \\  & =3\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
